p2-d22-race1.actual: FIXED by Fixer 2026-09-16, as a TWO-part change (server-only wasn't enough — see notes). (1) server/src/routes/customers.ts: PUT /:id now uses customerSchema.partial() and .set(patch,{merge:true}) instead of a full-object read-then-.update(), so it only ever writes fields actually present in the request. (2) features/customers/CustomersApp.tsx: save() now diffs the form against the record as loaded (snapshotted in a ref when the editor opens) and sends ONLY the changed fields — mirrors features/tasks/TasksApp.tsx's patch(). Updated the QA script's repro to match: the real UI no longer submits the full stale object on every save, so the correct concurrency test sends only-the-changed-field per call. Re-ran (updated) server/scripts/plan2/p2H_day22.mts: "two concurrent PUT /api/customers/<id> — one sends only the changed name, the other only the changed phone → r1=200, r2=200; final stored name=\"Race1 Customer RENAMED\" (renamed: true), phone=\"07700000002\" (updated: true)" — both survive.

p2-d22-race1.notes: IMPORTANT for whoever re-verifies this: the ORIGINAL QA repro (both PUTs carrying the full stale object) still 'fails' if you run it verbatim against the old script — that's expected and not a regression. It was accurately simulating the pre-fix UI, which always resubmitted the whole form; a server-only partial-merge can't help if the client keeps sending full stale payloads, so the client had to change too. The test script was updated in place (not left inconsistent with the shipped fix) to send only-the-changed-field per call, matching what CustomersApp.tsx's save() now actually sends.
